name: mining_anchors
purpose: The independently-published workings the geology affinity model was scored against, reduced to what a reader needs to resolve each one: coordinate, observation year, resource, the original dataset's own id, and where to look it up. Not a mining inventory and not our data.
notice: These are OTHER ORGANISATIONS' observations, cited here under the attribution and terms named on each feature -- five fields per point, which is a citation and not a substitute for anybody's dataset. `terms` = 'unstated' means the publisher granted no licence: attribute them, and check before redistributing further. They are evidence that the affinity layer was checked against reality; they are not a prediction, a ranking or a claim that any other ground is barren.

sources.label: IPIS artisanal mine visits, Central African Republic
sources.attribution: International Peace Information Service (IPIS), curated open data

sources.label: IPIS ASM site survey, Tanzania
sources.attribution: International Peace Information Service (IPIS), Tanzania ASM mapping, DGD 2017-2019
sources.note: includes processing sites as well as workings; sitetype is carried in `observed` so a mill is not read as a pit

sources.label: Geological Survey of Tanzania occurrence register (GMIS)
sources.attribution: Geological Survey of Tanzania, Geological and Mineral Information System
sources.note: the same minerogenic programme that drew the Tanzania sheet compiled this register, so it is not arm's length; no observation date exists in the register

sources.label: NGA Tearline CAR mine census (Lobaye Invest permits)
sources.attribution: NGA Tearline / geoLab, College of William & Mary, published 2021-12-16
sources.note: an imagery census INSIDE eight mining permits, not a national survey; the resource is the mineral named in the permit, not one observed at the working, and no per-mine date exists

sources.label: ICMM Global Mining Dataset v1.5
sources.attribution: International Council on Mining and Metals, Global Mining Dataset v1.5
sources.note: industrial assets compiled from commercial registries, coordinates approximate; artisanal mining is absent by design, and closed mines carry no flag

sources.label: Mine sites recovered from Crisis Tracker incident reports
sources.attribution: Incident records: Crisis Tracker, a project of Invisible Children. The mine labelling and clustering are ours and must not be attributed to them.
sources.note: every site is on this list because an attack there was reported, so its coverage is attacks and not mining; the year is the last reported incident, not a survey date. Only materials a note says the site YIELDS are carried -- looted goods travel and are not evidence about the rock.

sources.label: OpenStreetMap mine, quarry, adit and mineshaft features
Tang & Werner (2023) global mining footprints, centroids
sources.note: no commodity and no date field exist in this dataset; resource and year are NULL for every row, and one mine is several polygons

sources.label: USGS major mineral deposits of Africa
sources.attribution: USGS OFR 2005-1294-E (Taylor et al. 2009), via the JRC Africa Knowledge Platform
sources.note: industrial-scale NAMED deposits, a different kind of claim from a visited artisanal pit; no observation date

withheld.label: ACLED conflict events (coverage context only)
withheld.why: ACLED's Content Usage Terms forbid ACLED rows in a public export. It was never a mining list: it describes how far our truth sets could reach, and a conflict count is not evidence that a place is mined.
